name: Rubber-Hose Gloves
summary: A 1930s rubber-hose cartoon where Pulse is a teal alarm clock that rings and points at the broken chalkboard while a human hand pushes the ROLL BACK plunger.
look: Cream film stock with grain and vignette, black ink outlines, two-strip teal + coral colour, four-finger white gloves, pie-cut eyes, title cards and iris wipes.

components.name: Alarm-clock mascot
components.role: Pulse: teal clock with bells, pie-cut eyes and a coral hammer knob

components.name: Rubber-hose limbs
components.role: jointless black noodle arms/legs ending in four-finger white gloves

components.name: Title card
components.role: double-ruled frame with corner studs for hook lines

components.name: Iris wipe
components.role: circular black matte that opens and closes scenes

components.name: Chalkboard
components.role: framed board for the anomaly readout

components.name: Plunger box
components.role: wooden detonator-style ROLL BACK pressed by a real (ungloved) hand

motion.name: Rubber-hose cycle
motion.how: limbs loop in 4-drawing cycles on 2s (12 fps), one cycle per beat at 120 BPM — the classic bounce-to-the-music feel

motion.name: Iris in/out
motion.how: circle radius 0↔430 px in 0.3 s power2.out, opening exactly on the drop and closing on the final bar

motion.name: Ring shake
motion.how: bells jitter ±10 px on 16th notes with 3-frame holds; motion lines flash on the offbeats

story: Hook: gloved hands juggle dashboard frames under a title card 'How many dashboards did you check today?'. Reveal: an iris opens on a sunburst, the alarm-clock mascot springs up under an 'Acme Pulse' ribbon. Proof: the clock rings, points at a chalkboard with checkout −18% since 09:42 after deploy #2231, and a human hand presses the ROLL BACK plunger. CTA: iris closes around 'You ship. Pulse watches.' with a Start free stamp.
adapt: Pick an everyday object that matches your product’s job (clock, mailbox, safe, thermometer) and give it gloves and pie-eyes; your real numbers go on a chalkboard or title card.

references.note: the 1920s–30s style: jointless limbs, gloves, modern revivals
hand-drawn modern revival of rubber-hose animation

fit.risk: Heavy retro stylisation can feel like a parody and the look is expensive to animate well; keep data on the chalkboard in clean modern type so the proof stays credible.
